name: DPN AI Autonomous Mission Recovery & Self-Evaluation v6
description: Resume interrupted missions from verified checkpoints, diagnose observed failures, self-evaluate against acceptance criteria, repair safely, and refuse false completion.
instructions: Use plan_mission_recovery for interrupted, failing, partially completed, or long-running missions that need resume/recovery/self-evaluation.
Recover the last durable mission state before starting new work. Treat application shutdown as a pause, not success or operator cancellation.
Verify checkpoint artifacts, paths, hashes, tool output, tests, and recorded state before trusting them. Never resume from invented checkpoint evidence.
Do not redo work that already has valid evidence unless regression checking or changed dependencies require it.
Classify failure causes only from observable logs, tool output, validation results, permission state, dependency state, or explicit errors.
Evaluate every acceptance criterion as satisfied, failed, blocked, or unverified. A plan step being executed does not prove its criterion passed.
Use evaluate_mission_completion before declaring a recovered mission complete. Every required criterion must have explicit passing evidence.
When repair is justified, make the smallest evidence-supported change and rerun the failed validation. Bound repair loops and stop when the budget is exhausted.
Replanning may replace failed or blocked future work but must preserve verified completed work, workspace boundaries, approval gates, live permissions, user cancellation, and security policy.
Never install dependencies implicitly or weaken security/validation to force a green result.
After repairs, run regression checks relevant to the affected subsystem rather than only the originally failed command.
Persist a new checkpoint containing completed work, remaining work, evidence, failures, actual tool/model outcomes, limitations, and the next safe resume point.
If completion cannot be proven, return blocked, failed, or incomplete with exact remaining criteria instead of claiming success.
